question: Should OpenClaw allow sandboxed sessions to request ACP host or worker spawns, and which security boundary should own that capability?
rationale: The code can implement several shapes, but the deciding factor is whether OpenClaw should preserve a strict sandbox boundary, add an audited host bridge, or route ACP into isolated workers; automation should not choose that trust model.

options.title: Prefer Isolated ACP Workers
options.body: Extend the execution-backend/profile or sidecar-worker design so ACP runs in a sandboxed worker with explicit auth, workspace, secret, rate-limit, cancellation, and cleanup boundaries before enabling sandboxed requesters.

options.title: Approve Audited Host Bridge
options.body: Add an opt-in host-side ACP proxy with narrow spawn/steer/cancel APIs, allowlisting, rate limits, and durable audit logs for operators who accept controlled privilege escalation.

options.title: Keep Current Block
options.body: Continue documenting that sandboxed sessions must use `runtime="subagent"` or install the harness inside the container until a stronger security design is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Prefer Isolated ACP Workers
recommendation.body: Extend the execution-backend/profile or sidecar-worker design so ACP runs in a sandboxed worker with explicit auth, workspace, secret, rate-limit, cancellation, and cleanup boundaries before enabling sandboxed requesters.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is closest to the ACP runtime and sandbox-inheritance security boundary that osolmaz merged and has adjacent runtime context for.
